name: Next.js App Router
fit: React application shell with server rendering, nested layouts and a backend for the frontend.
tradeoff: Keep secrets in server modules. Move long runs into a durable execution service.
prompt: Render the run header on the server and hydrate only the interactive graph and controls.

name: React
fit: Composable client islands for a rich operator interface.
tradeoff: A high-frequency trace can re-render the whole screen if state lives at the root.
prompt: Subscribe each node to its own projected state and keep immutable event records outside the view.

name: Vite
fit: Fast development and a static SPA when an existing API owns all business logic.
tradeoff: Authentication callbacks, routing and deployment rewrites are separate choices.
prompt: Ship the SPA from a CDN and point its typed API client at the regional backend.

name: Angular
fit: Opinionated framework for teams with an established Angular platform and design system.
tradeoff: React graph and chat widgets need equivalents or explicit integration boundaries.
prompt: Use the existing Angular shell, routing and forms. Keep the run-event schema framework independent.

name: Nuxt
fit: Full-stack option for Vue teams needing server routes and hybrid rendering.
tradeoff: Budget for Vue-native graph, form and component choices.
prompt: Keep the same tenant-scoped HTTP and event contracts behind a Nuxt application.

name: Tailwind CSS
fit: Fast implementation of tokens, layouts, breakpoints and state styles.
tradeoff: Unrestricted utility choices fragment color, spacing and density.
prompt: Expose semantic CSS variables for canvas, surface, focus, critical, and selection. Use logical spacing for RTL.

name: shadcn/ui
fit: Editable source components for a branded product with dialogs, sheets, comboboxes and sidebars.
tradeoff: Your team owns edits and upstream merges. Record the chosen primitive family.
prompt: Start with the sidebar, command, sheet and dialog components. Implement the same focus and density rules in each.

name: Base UI
fit: Headless React behavior under a custom skin, including the default foundation for new shadcn projects.
tradeoff: Composition and slot APIs differ across primitive families.
prompt: Choose the Base UI shadcn preset. Use documented trigger composition and test the focus return path.

name: Radix Primitives
fit: Unstyled interactive primitives for an existing Radix-based component library.
tradeoff: Mixing dialog or popover systems complicates portals, stacking and focus.
prompt: Keep the existing Radix primitives for menus, dialogs and tooltips and share one overlay policy.

name: React Aria Components
fit: Accessible behavior for custom collections and internationalized forms with complex keyboard navigation.
tradeoff: The team still owns styling, localization QA and assistive-technology testing.
prompt: Use React Aria for the date range and selection controls. Test Arabic labels, keyboard selection and focus restoration.

name: Material UI
fit: A consistent React product suite where Material patterns are already familiar.
tradeoff: A proprietary visual identity may require theme work. Evaluate MUI X editions separately.
prompt: Use one MUI theme for data entry, alerts and navigation. Document density and touch target overrides.

name: Mantine
fit: Broad React component coverage for internal admin apps with a small frontend team.
tradeoff: A second full component kit increases CSS and visual drift.
prompt: Build the settings console on Mantine and use its theme primitives throughout the form.

name: Carbon Design System
fit: Enterprise information density, data tables, accessibility guidance and consistent component vocabulary.
tradeoff: Adopting its visual language works best when product and design agree to it.
prompt: Refer to Carbon table selection, toolbar placement and side panels for operator workflows.

name: Motion for React
fit: State-driven layout, entry and exit transitions for a live interface.
tradeoff: Repeated layout animations compete with streaming updates. Respect reduced motion.
prompt: Animate a handoff once when its persisted edge event arrives. Keep a static arrow and text for reduced motion.

name: GSAP
fit: Seekable timelines for replay, with MotionPathPlugin for packets moving along curved SVG edges and ScrollTrigger for explainers.
tradeoff: Use one clock per property. Keep live arrival order independent of presentation time and review licensing for redistribution.
prompt: Map a recorded event sequence to timeline labels. Seek deterministically, restore node state on scrub and use a stationary directional label under reduced motion.

name: Rive
fit: Designer-authored stateful animation for a device, robot or illustrated process.
tradeoff: Requires an art asset, renderer budget and fallback semantics.
prompt: Bind the device visual to idle, processing and fault states. Publish equivalent text and a static fallback.

name: React Flow
fit: Interactive dependency graphs with custom nodes, selection, pan and zoom.
tradeoff: Layout and execution come from separate systems. Dense graphs need a timeline alternative.
prompt: Use @xyflow/react for read-only execution topology. Inspect a node by mouse or keyboard and match its timeline row.

name: ELK.js
fit: Automatic graph layout for branching plans or nested dependencies.
tradeoff: Repeated layout causes jitter and main-thread stalls.
prompt: Compute the layered layout in a worker on topology changes, then animate only the active edge.

name: Apache ECharts
fit: Linked time-series views, distributions and operational metrics.
tradeoff: Highly configurable charts require deliberate units, missing-data handling and accessible summaries.
prompt: Show queue wait and tool latency separately with p50 and p95. Provide a table for the selected time window.

name: MapLibre GL JS
fit: Map rendering for fleet, incident and site operations with your own style and tile choices.
tradeoff: Budget tile hosting, attribution and offline behavior separately.
prompt: Cluster sites by zoom. Selecting a marker and selecting its table row must open the same incident.

name: deck.gl
fit: GPU-accelerated geospatial layers for dense telemetry and paths.
tradeoff: Payload volume and GPU memory matter on low-end devices.
prompt: Add a time-windowed trajectory layer over the basemap and bound the number of rendered points.

name: React Three Fiber
fit: React renderer for a real 3D inspection task or digital twin.
tradeoff: 3D scenes add asset weight and GPU load. Define what decision needs the extra dimension.
prompt: Lazy-load the equipment view only on inspection, show loading state and offer a labeled 2D schematic.

name: TanStack Table
fit: Headless sorting, filtering and column models for queues built to your own design system.
tradeoff: You implement semantics, keyboard behavior, pagination UI and rendering.
prompt: Build a URL-filtered queue with stable row IDs and preserve the selected run when the sort changes.

name: TanStack Virtual
fit: Window long timelines and lists whose DOM cost becomes measurable.
tradeoff: Dynamic row heights and keyboard focus require testing.
prompt: Virtualize the event history, preserve the scroll anchor, and announce new rows without stealing focus.

name: AG Grid
fit: Spreadsheet-like analysis with commercial options for pivoting, grouping and server-side row models.
tradeoff: Check feature entitlement and licensing before choosing a grid module.
prompt: Use Enterprise only when pivot or the Server-Side Row Model is required and licensed. Specify large-data tests.

name: TanStack Query
fit: Server-state cache for authorized run lists, evidence and details.
tradeoff: A query cache shared across tenant switches can expose stale data.
prompt: Scope query keys to tenant and run, cancel stale queries on switch, and clear tenant data on sign-out.

name: React Hook Form
fit: Performance-conscious forms for case intake and reviewer decisions.
tradeoff: Client errors can drift from server validation.
prompt: Validate on submit with the shared schema, retain typed fields after a server error and focus the first invalid control.

name: Zod
fit: Runtime schemas at TypeScript boundaries for inputs, tool arguments and streamed events.
tradeoff: Shape validation alone grants no authority over an object.
prompt: Parse unknown payloads server-side, authorize referenced resources and reject unsupported event versions.

name: XState
fit: Explicit client state machines for reconnect, review and replay controls.
tradeoff: Duplicating the backend workflow in the browser creates conflicting states.
prompt: Model only view modes and connection states in XState. Derive business status from ordered events.

name: AI Elements
fit: Editable UI components for messages, tool output, sources and AI-assisted workflows.
tradeoff: Map runtime events to view models. Review components that display sensitive details.
prompt: Use a tool card with name, elapsed time, scrubbed input summary and result link. Keep approvals server-authorized.

name: assistant-ui
fit: Conversation-first React UI with thread primitives and runtime integration.
tradeoff: A chat thread alone gives poor visibility into parallel work.
prompt: Attach a thread to the selected run and preserve links from each tool result to its evidence.

name: CopilotKit
fit: Embedded copilots that read scoped application context and expose interactive actions.
tradeoff: Define exactly which state and actions a user session may share.
prompt: Mount a contextual copilot on one case. Confirm each write through the same server policy as a normal button.

name: AG-UI
fit: Event protocol between different agent runtimes and interactive clients.
tradeoff: Choose supported event types and version an adapter to the business event log.
prompt: Map run, tool and lifecycle updates through an adapter and preserve your own replay cursor.

name: json-render
fit: Schema-constrained generative UI from a registered component and action catalog.
tradeoff: Models need a small catalog, strict validation and an ordinary fallback for invalid specs.
prompt: Allow Summary, EvidenceList and ApprovalRequest. Validate props and authorize any action on the server.

name: A2UI
fit: Declarative UI descriptions for an agent to request widgets across renderer implementations.
tradeoff: Confirm schema and renderer compatibility before promising a cross-client feature.
prompt: Negotiate a supported catalog, reject unknown actions and provide a generic read-only fallback.

name: Streamdown
fit: Streaming Markdown rendering when prose arrives incrementally.
tradeoff: Treat links and embedded content as untrusted and constrain optional heavy renderers.
prompt: Keep partial Markdown readable, restrict link schemes, and render code as text until the fence is closed.

name: eve
fit: Integrated TypeScript harness for Vercel-first apps with durable runs, subagents and approvals.
tradeoff: Recently reached 1.0. Validate region, export, run retention, sandbox limits and your recovery path.
prompt: Use eve as the sole run owner. Map its tool, approval and completion transitions to a durable public event log.

name: LangGraph
fit: Explicit state graphs for conditional routing, parallel branches, joins and human review.
tradeoff: You own state schemas, checkpoint storage, tool idempotency and schema migrations.
prompt: Use a persistent checkpointer, stable thread IDs and explicit branch joins. Resume an interrupted run after a worker restart.

name: Deep Agents
fit: A higher-level harness on LangGraph for planning, context offload and subagent delegation.
tradeoff: File tools and shared memory widen the permissions surface.
prompt: Give the research specialist a run-scoped workspace, read-only tools and bounded delegation.

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
fit: Lightweight agents, handoffs, tools and tracing for teams already using OpenAI integrations.
tradeoff: Choose durable storage and an execution recovery strategy for long business processes.
prompt: Define triage and specialist handoffs, narrow tool grants and a typed final output. Test provider timeout and replay.

name: Vercel AI SDK
fit: TypeScript model calls, tools and streaming for a bounded application agent.
tradeoff: A tool loop still needs persistence, retry ownership and an explicit stopping policy.
prompt: Use an allowlisted provider/model and typed tools. Bound steps, elapsed time and spend.

name: Mastra
fit: Integrated TypeScript agents and explicit workflows for a Node team.
tradeoff: Evaluate the hosting adapter, persistence and upgrade path together.
prompt: Define a typed workflow with an evidence step and suspended review, then prove resume after redeploy.

name: Pydantic AI
fit: Typed Python dependencies and outputs for model-assisted domain workflows.
tradeoff: Structured output can still be factually wrong. Track outcome quality on real examples.
prompt: Return a typed recommendation with evidence IDs, verify those IDs and score support for each claim.

name: Microsoft Agent Framework
fit: .NET and Python agent workflows for Microsoft-platform teams and existing Semantic Kernel or AutoGen estates.
tradeoff: Migration and feature support differ by language and connector.
prompt: Use the supported workflow primitives in one language. Pin connector versions and test checkpoint recovery.

name: Google ADK
fit: Agents, tools and workflow composition for teams using the Google agent ecosystem.
tradeoff: Check session persistence, identity propagation and host-specific behavior.
prompt: Give each specialist a bounded toolset and persist sessions in the approved regional service.

name: Claude Agent SDK
fit: Tool-capable Claude agents for research, document work and controlled coding workflows.
tradeoff: Permission mode, tool allowlists, execution environment and credentials need deliberate ownership.
prompt: Give one worker an isolated workspace and approved read tools. Capture artifact references and redact traces.

name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
fit: Choose a managed agent harness or host your own agent code in AgentCore Runtime.
tradeoff: The managed harness and runtime expose different control points. Check regional availability by service.
prompt: Document which layer owns the loop, where sessions live and how tool calls inherit scoped identity.

name: MCP
fit: Standard interface for tool and resource servers shared across clients.
tradeoff: Protocol compatibility and tool discovery do not establish tenant or action authority.
prompt: Pin a protocol revision, verify server identity, allowlist tools, and bind credentials to the tenant.

name: A2A
fit: Interoperability between independently deployed agents with task lifecycles.
tradeoff: In-process specialists rarely justify protocol negotiation or remote identity overhead.
prompt: Use it only across a real service boundary. Validate agent identity, capabilities, timeouts and artifacts.

name: Vercel AI Gateway
fit: Managed routing across model providers behind one gateway.
tradeoff: Fallback can change region, data policy, model behavior and cost.
prompt: Allowlist eligible fallback providers per data class and record the actual provider and model per call.

name: LiteLLM
fit: Gateway/proxy with a common model interface for a team operating its own routing layer.
tradeoff: You own the proxy's availability, upgrades, keys and policy.
prompt: Assign virtual credentials by application and tenant. Reject unapproved fallbacks and log attributed spend.

name: Vercel Sandbox
fit: Isolated compute for an agent that genuinely needs to execute generated code.
tradeoff: Bound network, lifetime, artifacts and credential exposure per execution.
prompt: Start a short-lived sandbox with scoped inputs. Copy approved artifacts out, then expire the environment.

name: E2B
fit: Independent sandbox service for model-generated code or data analysis.
tradeoff: Evaluate image lineage, region, egress controls and session cleanup.
prompt: Use a prepared image, minimal file mounts, bounded time and an audited artifact-export path.

name: Temporal
fit: Durable business workflows spanning outages, external systems and long human waits.
tradeoff: Deterministic workflow code, activity idempotency and worker versioning are operational commitments.
prompt: Make Temporal the workflow owner. Put all network and model calls into bounded activities.

name: Inngest
fit: Event-triggered durable steps and background work for application teams.
tradeoff: Choose a single retry owner per side effect. Test event re-delivery and concurrency limits.
prompt: Give each step a stable name and each logical effect a deduplication key. Exercise a duplicate trigger.

name: Workflow SDK
fit: Durable TypeScript functions and steps, including the execution substrate used by eve.
tradeoff: Check upgrade, retention and deployment adapter behavior for the chosen host.
prompt: Persist run references and use durable waits for review. If using eve, keep approvals in its owning workflow.

name: FastAPI
fit: Typed HTTP boundary for a Python agent or retrieval service.
tradeoff: Long work in a request handler consumes capacity and is vulnerable to disconnects.
prompt: Return 202 with a run ID, validate scope, enqueue durably, and expose a cursor-based event endpoint.

name: NestJS
fit: Structured Node API with modules and dependency injection for larger backend teams.
tradeoff: A separate API service adds deployment and tracing overhead.
prompt: Organize by case, approval and execution modules and validate inputs at each external boundary.

name: OpenAPI
fit: Describe HTTP endpoints and generate consistent clients for UI and integrations.
tradeoff: Breaking response changes need compatibility and contract tests.
prompt: Specify Run, Evidence, Approval and Problem responses. Include 403, 409 and idempotent retry examples.

name: AsyncAPI
fit: Document event channels, payloads and producer/consumer contracts across teams.
tradeoff: A specification cannot enforce delivery order or deduplication.
prompt: Publish event versions, delivery guarantees and per-run ordering. Reject unknown breaking versions.

name: C4 model
fit: Architecture notation for context, containers and component ownership.
tradeoff: Dense component diagrams obscure operational boundaries.
prompt: Draw browser, BFF, worker, database, IdP and model boundary. Label the owner and protocol of each crossing.

name: PostgreSQL
fit: System of record for tenants, runs, approvals, events and effect receipts with row-level policies.
tradeoff: Table owners and BYPASSRLS roles can bypass policies. Model worker privileges explicitly.
prompt: Enable tenant policies and use scoped roles. Test cross-tenant access on the API, event stream and evidence.

name: Drizzle ORM
fit: Typed SQL access and migrations for a TypeScript/Postgres application.
tradeoff: Migration lock time and RLS behavior still need database-level testing.
prompt: Use reviewed migrations and verify a least-privilege application role on a restored production-sized database.

name: pgvector
fit: Vector retrieval beside relational metadata when Postgres already stores your knowledge base.
tradeoff: Approximate retrieval under restrictive filters can hurt recall. Evaluate tenant-specific queries.
prompt: Apply document ACLs and tenant filters, measure recall at k and cite stable chunk IDs.

name: NATS JetStream
fit: Persistent streams when several workers or independent consumers must replay domain events.
tradeoff: At-least-once scenarios require consumer deduplication and capacity planning.
prompt: Set explicit retention, ack policy and consumer lag alarms. Keep the authoritative run sequence in the store.

name: Amazon S3
fit: Object storage for large evidence files and exported artifacts.
tradeoff: Signed URLs are bearer access. Decide expiry, retention, region and versioning.
prompt: Store opaque object references in events and mint short-lived downloads after authorization.

name: Transactional outbox
fit: Commit a domain change and its pending message in the same database transaction.
tradeoff: Dispatch can deliver duplicates. Consumers must tolerate retries.
prompt: Insert the run and outbox record atomically, publish after commit, and reconcile unacknowledged messages.

name: Server-sent events
fit: One-way browser delivery of ordered run updates alongside ordinary HTTP commands.
tradeoff: Connection limits, proxy buffering and cursor gaps vary by host.
prompt: Send event IDs, heartbeat, resume cursor and snapshot fallback. Recheck authorization on reconnect.

name: OpenTofu
fit: Versioned infrastructure for repeatable private-network or enterprise deployments.
tradeoff: Remote state is sensitive and needs restricted access and locking.
prompt: Provision separate stage and production with encrypted state and reviewed plans.

name: GitHub Actions OIDC
fit: Short-lived cloud credentials for build and deployment jobs.
tradeoff: Overbroad trust conditions can grant credentials to unintended jobs.
prompt: Restrict trust to the correct repository, workflow/environment and audience. Pin third-party actions.

name: OpenFeature
fit: Vendor-neutral flag evaluation for progressive rollout and a circuit-breaking product switch.
tradeoff: Flag evaluation must have a safe default when the provider fails.
prompt: Gate the new harness version by tenant cohort, record the variant on every run, and support rollback.

name: Storybook
fit: Isolated component states, interaction stories and design review.
tradeoff: A story can hide backend and reconnect failures. Pair it with a browser integration test.
prompt: Create an approval story for pending, expired, rejected and already handled states.

name: Playwright
fit: Browser verification across run creation, review and reconnection.
tradeoff: Time-based sleeps make event-driven tests brittle.
prompt: Wait for event-derived UI states and assert the same run after reload. Capture traces on failure.

name: axe-core for Playwright
fit: Automated accessibility checks within exercised screens.
tradeoff: Manual keyboard, screen reader, zoom and RTL testing remain necessary.
prompt: Check the dialog open state and completed trace, then manually verify focus return and a nonvisual handoff.

name: Grafana k6
fit: Load testing APIs, streams and queues against explicit workload assumptions.
tradeoff: Synthetic throughput without a representative tenant mix is misleading.
prompt: Test bursts from one tenant while measuring another tenant's admission latency and run completion.

name: OpenTelemetry
fit: Correlated traces, metrics and logs across BFF, workflow and model gateway.
tradeoff: Avoid tenant IDs in unbounded metric labels and scrub sensitive span attributes.
prompt: Propagate trace context across queues. Record wait, tool time and model time as separate spans.

name: Langfuse
fit: Agent traces, prompt versions, datasets and evaluation results.
tradeoff: Model inputs, outputs and traces can be sensitive. Configure sampling, redaction and retention.
prompt: Tag each result with workflow, prompt, model and dataset version. Compare cost per successful case.

name: Promptfoo
fit: Repeatable evaluation suites comparing prompts, providers and application outcomes.
tradeoff: Model-judged scores need human calibration. Keep deterministic controls separate.
prompt: Evaluate route, tool allowlist and evidence correctness against labeled cases and output a CI report.

name: OpenID Connect
fit: Federated identity for enterprise login through the organization's identity provider.
tradeoff: Identity alone does not authorize access to a tenant's records.
prompt: Validate issuer and audience, map tenant membership server-side, and renew the session on sensitive decisions.

name: Keycloak
fit: Self-managed identity and federation for teams with the operational capacity.
tradeoff: Owning the IdP adds patching, availability and recovery obligations.
prompt: Integrate a separate test realm and exercise role withdrawal, session expiry and logout propagation.

name: OpenFGA
fit: Relationship-based checks for shared cases, delegated reviewers and hierarchical access.
tradeoff: Relationship writes and caching introduce consistency questions at revocation.
prompt: Represent reviewer and viewer relationships on cases. Recheck write permission immediately before execution.

name: Open Policy Agent
fit: Contextual policy decisions outside model prompts and application conditionals.
tradeoff: Policy distribution, decision logging and fail-closed behavior need owners.
prompt: Gate tool invocation using subject, tenant, action, resource and approval state. Persist the policy version.

name: Vault
fit: Central secrets management where teams need scoped credentials and rotation.
tradeoff: Plan how workloads authenticate, renew leases and behave during an outage.
prompt: Use workload identity to retrieve scoped secrets. Never pass raw secrets through prompts or user traces.

name: OWASP ASVS
fit: Verification requirements for prioritizing application security controls and tests.
tradeoff: A checklist needs traceable evidence, applicability and ownership.
prompt: Map applicable requirements to tests, evidence links and accountable owners for this app.

name: OWASP agentic and GenAI guidance
fit: Threat categories for agent tools, autonomy, identities and delegated work.
tradeoff: Pair threat descriptions with preventive controls and release evidence.
prompt: Threat-model untrusted retrieved content, excessive agency and over-scoped access. Test the intended denial paths.

name: Semgrep
fit: Static analysis for unsafe patterns in generated and handwritten source.
tradeoff: Rules need tuning and owners to prevent high-noise gates.
prompt: Review new high-confidence findings on changed code and record time-limited, owned exceptions.

name: Trivy
fit: Scan built artifacts and infrastructure configuration for known issues.
tradeoff: Scan results depend on advisory freshness, artifact scope and configuration.
prompt: Scan the release image digest and IaC, record the scanner database time and triage actionable findings.

name: CycloneDX
fit: Standard bill-of-materials format for dependencies and shipped artifacts.
tradeoff: Generating an SBOM does not prove the release came from the trusted build.
prompt: Attach an SBOM to the release digest and verify it identifies the dependencies actually shipped.

name: Sigstore Cosign
fit: Sign and verify artifact identity and attestations in the release pipeline.
tradeoff: A valid signature still needs a trusted issuer and expected signing identity.
prompt: At deployment verify the artifact digest, expected workflow identity and issuer before promotion.

name: SLSA
fit: Supply-chain framework for evaluating build provenance and integrity.
tradeoff: Choose a target level and verify its actual requirements before making assurance claims.
prompt: Record source revision, builder identity and provenance verification alongside each release.

name: Anime.js
fit: SVG path drawing, morphing and object-on-path motion for custom diagrams.
tradeoff: Choose it for a bespoke diagram with a defined DOM owner. Avoid two animation engines writing the same property.
prompt: Animate a single envelope along the committed edge and clear it on completion or seek.

name: Web Animations API
fit: Native browser animation control for simple transitions and playback using a small dependency budget.
tradeoff: A path layout, timeline model and React lifecycle cleanup are your responsibility.
prompt: Animate the committed handoff in the browser and cancel the animation when the view unmounts or the cursor jumps.

name: D3 transitions
fit: Data joins and interpolated transitions for custom span waterfalls, distribution views and changing metrics.
tradeoff: Give D3 ownership of a bounded rendering subtree and stable span keys.
prompt: Build a duration waterfall keyed by span ID, preserve row order and update only the bars whose timestamps changed.

name: PixiJS
fit: A GPU-backed overlay for many simultaneous packet sprites or dense telemetry visuals.
tradeoff: Profile first. Use an accessible DOM inspector and keep GPU coordinates in sync with pan and zoom.
prompt: Render only visible, sampled transfer sprites; pause the ticker in background tabs and retain exact counts in the event list.

name: Sigma.js
fit: WebGL network exploration when the problem is a large network of relationships.
tradeoff: Rich editable HTML nodes and form-heavy operator workflows favor a different renderer.
prompt: Map the service dependency network at overview zoom and drill into one run for its exact sequence and decisions.

name: dotLottie-web
fit: Playback of authored vector motion assets for reusable illustrations and state cues.
tradeoff: An asset alone cannot encode changing topology, payloads or audit semantics.
prompt: Bind a short completion or fault asset to a committed state. Preserve visible status text and offer a still frame.

name: SvelteKit
fit: Server-rendered Svelte workspaces with forms and per-route loading.
tradeoff: Choose the deployment adapter early; streaming and server capabilities depend on the host.
prompt: Enhance a case form progressively, then test it with JavaScript disabled and with a validation error.

name: Astro
fit: A content-heavy documentation estate with occasional interactive components.
tradeoff: Hydrating every island gives away the lightweight delivery advantage.
prompt: Render reference pages as static HTML and hydrate only the diagram inspector.

name: TanStack Router
fit: Type-safe routing and shareable filter state in a React SPA.
tradeoff: The team owns the API and server-rendering integration it selects.
prompt: Represent queue filters and selected case as validated search parameters. Test a copied deep link.

name: Ant Design
fit: Dense business forms and administration workflows for a React team.
tradeoff: Translating a bespoke brand into the component system takes design ownership.
prompt: Specify table density, field validation, empty states and locale formatting in one theme.

name: Fluent UI
fit: An application that needs to feel familiar in the Microsoft ecosystem.
tradeoff: Check component coverage separately across React and web-component implementations.
prompt: Use the native Fluent patterns for task navigation, commands and contextual detail.

name: Spectrum
fit: An established design language with detailed interaction and accessibility guidance.
tradeoff: Design guidance and the chosen React implementation can differ in coverage.
prompt: Map date, selection and error semantics to the matching implementation before committing the design.

name: PatternFly
fit: Platform administration, cluster operations and dense resource inventory.
tradeoff: A mature admin vocabulary can still need domain-specific content and navigation.
prompt: Give resource status, namespace and last observed time separate fields in the inventory.

name: USWDS
fit: Public-service experiences needing clear forms and accessible layout guidance.
tradeoff: Check the service's own accessibility, language and brand obligations.
prompt: Use one question per decision and show corrective text that identifies the field and recovery action.

name: GOV.UK Design System
fit: Transactional services involving eligibility, application, review and confirmation.
tradeoff: Adapt local policy and language and retain the user's own visual identity.
prompt: Use a check-answers pattern before submission and a confirmation reference afterwards.

name: Floating UI
fit: Positioning an anchored inspector, tooltip or contextual menu in complex layouts.
tradeoff: Positioning alone does not supply dialog semantics or a focus policy.
prompt: Keep the inspector visible near the selected item on scroll and test Escape and focus return.

name: Ariakit
fit: A custom React design system with accessible menu, combobox and dialog behavior.
tradeoff: Visual treatment, integration testing and component composition are team responsibilities.
prompt: Test a long combobox with a keyboard, a screen reader and an input-method editor.

name: Headless UI
fit: Unstyled accessible components for an existing Tailwind-based interface.
tradeoff: Avoid mixing separate overlay stacks across teams without a shared focus contract.
prompt: Use the dialog primitive for review and restore focus to the invoking queue action.

name: Recharts
fit: Conventional React dashboards with composable Cartesian charts.
tradeoff: High mark counts and bespoke interactions need device-level profiling.
prompt: Plot queue age and tool latency on separate charts with labeled units and a table alternative.

name: Observable Plot
fit: Exploratory operational charts where a concise statistical grammar is valuable.
tradeoff: Product-level interaction and persistent selection need surrounding state management.
prompt: Facet queue delay by region and include sample size for each distribution.

name: Vega-Lite
fit: Reusable declarative chart specs for linked operational analytics.
tradeoff: A generated chart specification still needs schema, dataset and URL restrictions.
prompt: Allow an approved chart schema and a bounded field catalog; fail gracefully on invalid encodings.

name: Cytoscape.js
fit: Network analysis and graph selection where topology matters more than form-like nodes.
tradeoff: Interactive complexity, layout cost and accessibility need separate design.
prompt: Filter services by neighborhood and link selected nodes to an equivalent textual dependency view.

name: Graphviz
fit: Reproducible static architecture and dependency diagrams from structured topology.
tradeoff: Large diagrams can become illegible despite automatic layout.
prompt: Split trust boundaries and runtime flows across diagrams. Label edge direction and protocol.

name: Mermaid
fit: Maintaining architecture, state and sequence diagrams beside design decisions.
tradeoff: Renderer capabilities differ between documentation hosts.
prompt: Use stable names and one decision per diagram. Verify rendering on the publishing target.

name: visx
fit: Bespoke React visualizations requiring control over scales and marks.
tradeoff: The team owns axes, legends, keyboard navigation and accessible explanations.
prompt: Build a tool-span waterfall with consistent time scales and links to textual span details.

name: Konva
fit: A canvas-based floor plan, equipment editor or layered inspection surface.
tradeoff: A canvas needs a parallel semantic interaction path and explicit hit testing.
prompt: Synchronize canvas selection with a keyboard-accessible equipment list.

name: Three.js
fit: A 3D inspection where orientation or occlusion changes an operator's decision.
tradeoff: Asset budget, GPU availability and camera controls affect actual usability.
prompt: Define the inspection question, lazy-load the model and provide a labeled 2D fallback.

name: View Transition API
fit: Shared visual continuity between a list item and its detail screen.
tradeoff: Check platform support and avoid two engines animating the same element.
prompt: Provide a plain navigation path and honor reduced motion when transitioning between case and detail.

name: FormatJS
fit: Localized messages, plural forms and dates for internationalized web applications.
tradeoff: Extracted keys and translations require an ownership and release workflow.
prompt: Format numeric counts by locale and keep opaque case identifiers untranslated.

name: i18next
fit: Runtime locale selection and resource namespaces across multiple clients.
tradeoff: Lazy-loaded namespaces can produce partial screens or fallback leaks.
prompt: Test a missing translation and language switch in the middle of an approval journey.

name: Style Dictionary
fit: Distributing design tokens to several web and native clients.
tradeoff: Build transforms can diverge by platform or silently change token meaning.
prompt: Produce light, dark and high-contrast outputs from semantic aliases and review visual diffs.

name: Design Tokens Community Group format
fit: A portable token exchange format between design tools and platform builds.
tradeoff: Validate tool support for the selected specification revision and alias behavior.
prompt: Specify semantic color and motion tokens once and validate aliases before generating platform values.

name: Kafka
fit: A durable event backbone for independent consumers and replayable streams.
tradeoff: Partitioning defines ordering scope; slow consumers and schema drift require operational tooling.
prompt: Key events by aggregate ID, version payloads and expose consumer lag and replay controls.

name: RabbitMQ
fit: Work queues and routing where acknowledgment and delivery behavior are explicit.
tradeoff: A retry can redeliver work already applied at the destination.
prompt: Declare queue ownership, retry deadlines, dead-letter routing and an idempotent consumer.

name: Apache Flink
fit: Stateful stream processing for time-windowed telemetry and late events.
tradeoff: State size, watermark strategy and checkpoint recovery need load tests.
prompt: Define event time, allowed lateness and the correction rule for an updated metric.

name: Debezium
fit: Change-data capture for downstream projections and integration feeds.
tradeoff: Schema evolution, initial snapshots and retained transaction logs require ownership.
prompt: Specify a bootstrap snapshot, durable offsets and recovery when a consumer falls behind retention.

name: Redis
fit: Low-latency cache and short-lived counters for an existing application.
tradeoff: Eviction, failover and stale authorization can change business behavior.
prompt: Scope cache keys to tenant and permission version. Test eviction and database fallback.

name: Valkey
fit: An open-source key-value service where a managed or self-hosted deployment is needed.
tradeoff: Verify client, command and service compatibility with the workload.
prompt: Set TTL and memory policy per use case and test read behavior during failover.

name: ClickHouse
fit: Analytical scans across append-heavy events, traces or telemetry.
tradeoff: Table order and ingestion shape drive query cost and correction behavior.
prompt: Model the primary time and tenant filters and benchmark the p95 dashboard query on production-shaped data.

name: DuckDB
fit: Embedded analytics over columnar files for reproducible investigations.
tradeoff: Concurrency and memory budgets differ from a shared analytical service.
prompt: Analyze a versioned Parquet snapshot and report sampling, filters and query time.

name: OpenSearch
fit: Search across indexed enterprise documents with filters and aggregations.
tradeoff: Index freshness and authorization propagation need explicit service objectives.
prompt: Apply tenant and document grants, record source revisions and test revoked-document search.

name: Qdrant
fit: A dedicated vector retrieval service for filtered semantic search.
tradeoff: Choosing an index, embedding revision and filter strategy requires a labeled retrieval set.
prompt: Benchmark recall and latency with restrictive tenant filters and realistic deletion frequency.

name: Apache Iceberg
fit: Large analytical tables that need snapshot history and schema evolution.
tradeoff: Catalog maintenance, compaction and expired snapshot cleanup have a cost.
prompt: Version the event schema and define the retention and compaction policy for archived runs.

name: gRPC
fit: Typed internal service calls and streaming across service boundaries.
tradeoff: Browser and proxy compatibility need a deliberate gateway or transport choice.
prompt: Set deadlines and cancellation, version protobuf fields compatibly and test service degradation.

name: GraphQL
fit: Multiple clients need different shapes of a shared domain graph.
tradeoff: Resolver authorization, query cost and per-field fan-out need controls.
prompt: Cap complexity and verify field-level authorization on sensitive case relationships.

name: CloudEvents
fit: A common envelope across event producers and transport adapters.
tradeoff: Domain schemas, delivery guarantees and tenant permissions remain application decisions.
prompt: Keep source, type, ID and payload schema stable across broker and HTTP transports.

name: JSON Schema
fit: Validating data at HTTP, workflow, tool and event boundaries.
tradeoff: Draft support and allowed keywords vary across validators and model providers.
prompt: Pin the dialect and reject unknown action types before a tool receives arguments.

name: Kubernetes
fit: A platform team needs scheduling, rollout and isolation controls for many services.
tradeoff: Operational overhead is substantial for a small service or simple website.
prompt: Specify resource requests, disruption budgets and worker drain behavior before choosing the cluster shape.

name: Argo CD
fit: Declarative application delivery from Git for Kubernetes environments.
tradeoff: Separately authorize repository writes, deployment promotion and secret access.
prompt: Show drift, require production promotion review and rehearse rollback of a worker revision.

name: Helm
fit: Packaging and configuring versioned Kubernetes applications.
tradeoff: Template complexity can hide environment-specific mistakes.
prompt: Render and check the production values in CI and document data migration dependencies.

name: Envoy
fit: Consistent edge or service-proxy behavior across a polyglot estate.
tradeoff: Timeout and retry policies can amplify work when also configured upstream.
prompt: Assign retry ownership and measure the effective end-to-end request deadline.

name: Dapr
fit: Common building blocks for services across different language runtimes.
tradeoff: Sidecar dependencies introduce another version, latency and recovery boundary.
prompt: Specify which pub/sub or state component is used and test its actual delivery semantics.

name: Backstage
fit: A developer portal for service ownership, documentation and templates.
tradeoff: Catalog accuracy needs integration with engineering ownership practices.
prompt: Expose the team's runbook, service owner, SLO and escalation path on one catalog record.

name: OpenAPI Generator
fit: Repeatable client generation for multiple API consumers.
tradeoff: Generator changes and hand edits create drift.
prompt: Pin the generator and schema revision and verify an older client against the new server.

name: LlamaIndex
fit: Ingestion and retrieval components for evidence-backed domain assistants.
tradeoff: A retrieval pipeline needs independent ACL enforcement and citation evaluation.
prompt: Link every returned chunk to its authorized source revision and measure recall.

name: Haystack
fit: Explicit search and generation pipelines with swappable components.
tradeoff: Pipeline flexibility can complicate component-level performance attribution.
prompt: Benchmark retrieval, reranking and generation independently against a fixed query set.

name: DSPy
fit: Optimizing typed language-model programs against a defined metric and examples.
tradeoff: An optimizer can improve a proxy metric while worsening a business outcome.
prompt: Use separate training and held-out sets and inspect failure slices before promoting the candidate.

name: CrewAI
fit: Role-based multi-agent coordination with explicit tasks and process choices.
tradeoff: More roles can add repeated work and compound cost.
prompt: Compare two specialists against a single-agent baseline and cap delegation depth.

name: Strands Agents
fit: Model-driven agents with composable tools for teams working in the AWS ecosystem.
tradeoff: Model-directed tools still need scoped credentials and explicit stop conditions.
prompt: Document the agent loop, model boundary, permitted tools and receipt requirements.

name: Semantic Kernel
fit: An installed Microsoft agent or plugin estate requiring maintenance or migration analysis.
tradeoff: Review the Microsoft Agent Framework migration path for new investment.
prompt: Inventory existing plugins, memory and workflows and test the target equivalent on representative cases.

name: Model Context Protocol Apps
fit: Interactive resources served from a tool experience to a compatible host.
tradeoff: Host support, isolation, authentication and renderer behavior need verification.
prompt: Define allowed UI actions and a text-only fallback for clients without the extension.

name: OpenAI Responses API
fit: Applications using OpenAI tools, structured responses and multi-step interactions.
tradeoff: Available tools and retention controls depend on model, account and configuration.
prompt: Map tool call and result identifiers to the business run without exposing provider secrets.

name: Claude Messages API
fit: Applications invoking Claude with typed content blocks and tools.
tradeoff: The client has to handle tool responses, continuation, failures and output validation.
prompt: Record the stop reason, validate each tool request and return a scoped tool result.

name: Cloudflare Workflows
fit: Durable execution aligned with a Workers deployment.
tradeoff: Review current step limits, retention and supported runtimes.
prompt: Suspend the workflow at a human wait and prove a worker redeploy preserves the pending decision.

name: AWS Step Functions
fit: AWS-native state machines coordinating managed services and business activities.
tradeoff: Choose workflow type and cost model for the actual duration and volume.
prompt: Model retries, timeouts, explicit compensation and correlation to the business case.

name: Azure Durable Functions
fit: Durable orchestration and external events in an Azure Functions estate.
tradeoff: Orchestrator replay constrains code and requires careful versioning.
prompt: Put non-deterministic I/O in activities and test an old approval after a new deployment.

name: Restate
fit: Durable service invocation and stateful workflows with explicit service boundaries.
tradeoff: Service-side durability does not make a non-idempotent external action safe.
prompt: Use a stable logical effect ID and reconcile destination receipts across retries.

name: Vitest
fit: Fast unit and component-level checks for Vite-oriented applications.
tradeoff: Mocked tests alone cannot verify browser semantics or actual deployments.
prompt: Test the event reducer against duplicates, gaps, terminal transitions and cursor rewind.

name: Testing Library
fit: User-oriented component tests written against accessible roles and names.
tradeoff: An accessible query passing still leaves full keyboard and screen-reader journeys to verify.
prompt: Select by role, submit an invalid field and verify the visible recovery message.

name: Mock Service Worker
fit: Reproducible request-level behavior for integration tests and component stories.
tradeoff: Keep mocks synchronized with the real API contract.
prompt: Model delayed responses, a denied decision and a stale version using the published schema.

name: Pact
fit: Consumer-driven integration contracts between independently released services.
tradeoff: A contract test covers interactions represented by the consumer and provider suites.
prompt: Verify both last production consumer and next consumer contracts before promoting the provider.

name: Lighthouse
fit: Repeatable lab audits of representative pages and constrained device profiles.
tradeoff: A one-off lab score cannot stand in for field measurements or manual accessibility review.
prompt: Run the same authenticated task on every candidate and investigate the largest regression.

name: web-vitals
fit: Measuring user-centric performance in real browser sessions.
tradeoff: Sampling and device mix can hide regressions for an important cohort.
prompt: Compare p75 responsiveness by route, device class and release cohort with privacy-safe labels.

name: Jaeger
fit: Distributed trace exploration for causality, overlapping spans and service latency.
tradeoff: Sampled traces leave gaps in authoritative business history.
prompt: Link a run to its trace and distinguish active tool time, queue delay and human wait.

name: Prometheus
fit: Time-series monitoring and alerts for capacity, rates and saturation.
tradeoff: High-cardinality identifiers multiply storage and query cost.
prompt: Track bounded dimensions on admission, queue age and outcomes. Keep per-case IDs in traces.

name: Grafana Tempo
fit: A trace backend integrated with dashboards and telemetry pipelines.
tradeoff: Storage, sampling and sensitive attributes require deliberate governance.
prompt: Find a slow run from a metric exemplar and inspect linked tool and worker spans.

name: Sentry
fit: Application errors, release regressions and related performance symptoms.
tradeoff: Configure scrubbing and consent before collecting sensitive context or replay.
prompt: Attach a safe release tag and route name to an error, then verify source maps and redaction.

name: Arize Phoenix
fit: Open-source tracing and evaluation for LLM and retrieval workflows.
tradeoff: Trace visibility requires privacy controls and calibrated human labels.
prompt: Compare groundedness and tool success by model, dataset version and retrieval strategy.

name: Ragas
fit: Evaluations of retrieval-augmented answers and evidence quality.
tradeoff: Judge-model scores can be biased or unstable across upgrades.
prompt: Hold evidence fixed, calibrate against human labels and report disagreement on hard examples.

name: OpenLLMetry
fit: LLM-specific instrumentation layered onto OpenTelemetry export pipelines.
tradeoff: Instrumentation can capture sensitive request or response content if left unchecked.
prompt: Define the content capture policy and verify a synthetic sensitive marker never reaches the exporter.

name: Great Expectations
fit: Checking batch or analytical data assumptions before dependent workflows consume it.
tradeoff: Freshness, business validity and expectation ownership still need agreement.
prompt: Quarantine an invalid batch, record the failing expectation and preserve last-known-good data.

name: OpenSLO
fit: A portable way to express service-level objectives and their indicators.
tradeoff: Backend capabilities and alert translation need testing in the actual monitoring system.
prompt: Define admission latency and successful completion as separate SLIs with agreed measurement windows.

name: OAuth 2.0 Security BCP
fit: A current baseline for evaluating delegated authorization flows and client behavior.
tradeoff: Map the recommendations to your client type, identity provider and supported flows.
prompt: Document redirect validation, token audience, PKCE and token storage for the selected client.

name: WebAuthn
fit: Public-key credentials for user authentication, including passkey-capable journeys.
tradeoff: Enrollment, recovery, device availability and accessibility affect adoption.
prompt: Design registration, sign-in, lost-device recovery and fallback ownership as one journey.

name: SCIM
fit: Tenant provisioning and deprovisioning between an enterprise IdP and SaaS.
tradeoff: Sync lag and group mappings complicate immediate access revocation.
prompt: Show how disabling a directory account revokes active access and queued approvals.

name: SPIFFE
fit: Portable workload identity across service boundaries.
tradeoff: A trust domain and attestation policy require an operating owner.
prompt: Name each worker identity and verify the audience and trust domain before granting a tool.

name: SPIRE
fit: Issuing and rotating identities for attested workloads in a SPIFFE deployment.
tradeoff: Trust bootstrap and agent availability are infrastructure dependencies.
prompt: Define node and workload attestation plus the behavior when identity renewal is unavailable.

name: Cedar
fit: Policy-as-code decisions using principals, actions, resources and context.
tradeoff: The application must supply correct entities and enforce every decision.
prompt: Evaluate a reviewer action against tenant, case, role and proposal revision immediately before the write.

name: Zanzibar model
fit: A reference design for relationship-based authorization at significant scale.
tradeoff: Consistency after permission changes matters as much as relationship modeling.
prompt: Explain revocation freshness and how nested membership is bounded and tested.

name: OpenBao
fit: Self-managed secret storage, dynamic credentials and leases where operational control is needed.
tradeoff: Recovery, unsealing, availability and rotation require a named team.
prompt: Describe workload login, scoped lease lifetime, revocation and an outage drill.

name: Kyverno
fit: Kubernetes admission and policy enforcement for cluster workloads.
tradeoff: An overly broad policy can block legitimate deployments or create noisy exceptions.
prompt: Start with an owned policy report, test known workloads and explicitly approve enforcement scope.

name: Falco
fit: Runtime event detection for containerized workloads and operating-system activity.
tradeoff: High-volume alerts need tuning, correlation and an investigation owner.
prompt: Map one approved detection to an incident runbook and measure false positives on normal batch jobs.

name: Syft
fit: Software bill of materials generation for built packages and images.
tradeoff: Source and final-image inventories can differ.
prompt: Generate an SBOM for the release digest and associate the artifact and build metadata.

name: OSV-Scanner
fit: Dependency vulnerability screening against machine-readable advisories.
tradeoff: Reachability and business exposure still require triage.
prompt: Record affected package, shipped artifact, advisory revision and the owner of a remediation decision.

name: OpenSSF Scorecard
fit: Comparing observable repository security practices before adopting a dependency.
tradeoff: Scores can lag or misrepresent project context and are insufficient on their own.
prompt: Review the underlying checks, maintainer activity, provenance and unresolved findings.

name: NIST Zero Trust Architecture
fit: A reference for resource-centric access decisions across users, devices and workloads.
tradeoff: A design principle requires an inventory of resources, policy points and actual enforcement.
prompt: Mark policy decision, enforcement, identity evidence and audit boundaries on the architecture diagram.

name: OWASP SAMM
fit: Assessing maturity and prioritizing improvements to a software security program.
tradeoff: Maturity levels measure practices and require evidence from teams.
prompt: Select an improvement under design, implementation or verification with owner, evidence and target date.

name: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
fit: Practical defensive reference material for sessions, authorization, uploads and logging.
tradeoff: Select guidance relevant to your stack and threat model.
prompt: Map three concrete controls to their enforcement location and a non-destructive acceptance check.

name: WCAG 2.2
fit: Designing and evaluating accessible web content against defined success criteria.
tradeoff: Conformance requires evaluation of actual journeys, components and supported technology.
prompt: Specify keyboard completion, visible focus, input assistance, zoom and motion alternatives for the core task.

name: ARIA APG
fit: Established keyboard interaction and semantics for widgets such as dialogs, tabs and grids.
tradeoff: Applying a role without its expected behavior can worsen accessibility.
prompt: Compare the custom dialog against the APG keyboard and focus pattern with real assistive technology.

name: WAI Easy Checks
fit: An introductory review of headings, contrast, text alternatives and keyboard behavior.
tradeoff: Preliminary checks cover only part of an accessibility evaluation.
prompt: Use the easy checks for triage, then schedule deeper manual coverage of the critical task.

name: GOV.UK Service Manual
fit: Researching, designing, operating and measuring end-to-end transactional services.
tradeoff: Adapt service ownership and channel assumptions to your organization.
prompt: Map the customer's goal, assisted channel, operational dependency and service outcome.

name: 18F Methods
fit: Practical methods for discovery, synthesis, prototyping and evaluation.
tradeoff: Choose the method around a decision and the evidence you need.
prompt: Write a research question, recruitment criteria, session protocol and how the findings change a decision.

name: HEART framework
fit: Translating product goals into experience signals and metrics.
tradeoff: A broad framework still needs a baseline, denominator and action threshold.
prompt: Map onboarding success to observable task completion, repeat use and a countermetric for support burden.

name: Nielsen usability heuristics
fit: A structured expert review of visibility, control, errors and consistency.
tradeoff: An expert critique cannot establish how frequently real users fail.
prompt: Attach a screen, user task, severity rationale and a proposed validation method to every issue.

name: Service blueprinting
fit: Connecting customer actions to frontstage responses, backstage work and support systems.
tradeoff: A blueprint needs owners and recovery paths at cross-team handoffs.
prompt: Trace a missed appointment from customer notification through agent review to confirmed resolution.

name: W3C internationalization
fit: Guidance for language metadata, directionality, multilingual layout and text handling.
tradeoff: Translation alone cannot establish bidirectional or locale behavior.
prompt: Verify mixed Arabic text, Latin case IDs, numbers, dates and keyboard navigation in context.

name: Microsoft Inclusive Design
fit: Identifying mismatches between human abilities, context and product assumptions.
tradeoff: The method works best with participation from people experiencing the exclusion.
prompt: Recruit across permanent, temporary and situational constraints and retest the highest-friction task.

name: PostHog
fit: Connect invitation, first useful action and repeat use in an event funnel.
tradeoff: Session replay can collect sensitive screen content. Decide which events the product needs and disable unnecessary capture.
prompt: Draft an event dictionary for the booking funnel, including the server event that proves success.

name: Amplitude
fit: Investigate activation and retention across cohorts with a managed analytics platform.
tradeoff: A change in event definitions can look like a change in customer behavior. Version definitions and compare both for an overlap period.
prompt: Compare repeat bookings for two onboarding cohorts using a fixed inclusion rule.

name: GrowthBook
fit: Evaluate variants and analyze product experiments against warehouse data.
tradeoff: Randomizing by user can mix experiences inside a shared customer account. Define the unit of assignment first.
prompt: Design a tenant-level experiment with a primary outcome, guardrail and plan for small cohorts.

name: Unleash
fit: Roll a capability out to defined cohorts with centrally managed feature flags.
tradeoff: Long-lived flags create untested combinations. Give each flag a removal date and an owner.
prompt: Describe how to disable new booking proposals while settling existing ones.

name: LaunchDarkly
fit: Manage targeted releases and flag evaluation across multiple services.
tradeoff: Plan for stale or unavailable configuration and confirm which controls your contract covers.
prompt: Provide safe defaults for a new tenant and an unavailable flag service.

name: OpenMeter
fit: Meter usage against a product dimension such as completed operations per account.
tradeoff: Usage records need stable subjects and event IDs. A technical retry should not become a second billable outcome.
prompt: Model two tool attempts, one final receipt and the resulting usage record.

name: FinOps FOCUS
fit: Normalize supported billing data when comparing infrastructure or provider spend.
tradeoff: A common cost schema cannot assign an invoice line to a customer outcome without an allocation key.
prompt: Map eligible invoice fields to tenant and workload, and put unallocated cost in a visible bucket.

name: FinOps unit economics
fit: Define the business unit when reviewing model, infrastructure and human handling costs.
tradeoff: A cheap completed call can belong to a case that never resolves. Count eligible cases and final outcomes separately.
prompt: Compute cost per verified resolution for the baseline and the proposed pilot.

name: GOV.UK Service Standard
fit: Review whether a service solves a whole problem across channels and can be operated reliably.
tradeoff: Applying the standard still requires user research and evidence from people operating the service.
prompt: Trace a failed online booking into assisted support and back to a single case record.

name: Google SRE Workbook on SLOs
fit: Translate a customer promise into a measurable service-level objective and error budget.
tradeoff: A fast API response can hide a long wait for the actual service outcome.
prompt: Define good and eligible events for timely booking confirmation, and name the owner when the budget is exhausted.

name: NIST AI RMF Playbook
fit: Organize model-risk decisions, measurement and accountability across product stakeholders.
tradeoff: The playbook supplies guidance. Approval, evidence and treatment of residual risk remain organizational decisions.
prompt: Assign an accountable owner and measurable outcome to the three largest risks in the pilot.

name: AWS SaaS Lens
fit: Review tenant onboarding, isolation and tenant-aware operations in a SaaS architecture.
tradeoff: Map the advice to your deployment and customer contracts, including where evidence lives.
prompt: Walk a noisy tenant, a revoked tenant and a tenant export through the proposed service.

name: Airbyte
fit: Ingest operational records into an analytical store using source and destination connectors.
tradeoff: Check incremental cursors, deletes and schema drift for each connector before trusting the copy.
prompt: Reconcile a changed appointment, a deletion and two syncs that overlap.

name: dbt
fit: Transform analytical data into documented, testable models for product reporting.
tradeoff: Late receipts change attribution. Version the metric and define when prior periods can be restated.
prompt: Build a unique case-level result from attempts, receipts and support closures.

name: OpenLineage
fit: Describe lineage between jobs, runs and datasets across participating systems.
tradeoff: Missing integrations leave gaps. Verify the path of a single record rather than assuming universal coverage.
prompt: Map the sources behind a changed pilot metric and mark any uninstrumented hop.

name: DataHub
fit: Catalog datasets, ownership and lineage for discovery and governance.
tradeoff: A stale owner or incomplete ingestion makes a search result misleading. Set a freshness expectation.
prompt: Find the owner of the booking metric, its underlying data and the last successful ingestion.

name: Flyway
fit: Manage versioned relational database migrations with an established migration workflow.
tradeoff: A migration history cannot make a destructive schema change reversible. Rehearse old-reader compatibility and restoration.
prompt: Stage an additive receipt column, backfill it and verify that the prior app version still works.

name: LangChain text splitters
fit: Split long source documents before retrieval while retaining logical sections where possible.
tradeoff: Overlapping chunks can inflate apparent recall. Score against unique source passages and revisions.
prompt: Compare two chunking rules on the same policy questions and count distinct relevant passages.

name: Docling
fit: Parse structurally complex source documents for retrieval and inspection.
tradeoff: Tables and scans need manual spot checks. Preserve document and page provenance through conversion.
prompt: Show whether a fee and its exception remain linked after parsing the source table.

name: vLLM
fit: Serve supported model weights when a team owns inference deployment and capacity.
tradeoff: Model license, hardware fit, idle capacity and operations can dominate the business case.
prompt: Estimate the utilization at which a regional deployment beats the managed endpoint on cost per accepted task.

name: DeepEval
fit: Write LLM evaluation tests alongside Python development and CI workflows.
tradeoff: Judge-based metrics need calibration. Keep deterministic checks for receipts and permissions.
prompt: Report a grader disagreement and one policy violation separately from the mean answer score.

name: Braintrust
fit: Compare experiments on versioned datasets and examine individual cases and traces.
tradeoff: Review retention and project access before sending production examples or prompts.
prompt: Compare the same 20 redacted cases and show the three outcomes that changed the release decision.

name: LangSmith
fit: Inspect traced executions and evaluate different versions against labeled examples.
tradeoff: Telemetry can include customer material. Choose export fields, sampling and retention explicitly.
prompt: Turn one reviewed failure into an offline case with a reference answer and authoritative final state.

name: Inspect AI
fit: Build repeatable model evaluation tasks with datasets, solvers and scorers in Python.
tradeoff: A benchmark task needs a fixture that reflects what your product is allowed to do.
prompt: Define a booking task with a simulated lookup tool and a scorer for false confirmations.

name: OpenCost
fit: Allocate Kubernetes infrastructure costs when teams share a cluster.
tradeoff: Shared idle capacity and provider charges outside the cluster need explicit treatment.
prompt: Show allocated, shared and uncovered costs before comparing two inference deployments.

name: uPlot
fit: Render compact time-series charts for event rates, latency or queue depth.
tradeoff: Charts need units, zoom behavior and an accessible summary. Keep high-cardinality labels out of the overview.
prompt: Plot actual queue age by time and provide the latest value, unit and timestamp in text.

name: vis-timeline
fit: Show ranges and point events for work that spans people, services and time zones.
tradeoff: Overlapping items and rescheduling need stable identifiers and explicit time-zone policy.
prompt: Show approval waits and tool attempts on separate rows and preserve their IDs after reconnect.

name: React Virtuoso
fit: Virtualize a long activity feed with variable-height rows.
tradeoff: New events should not pull an operator away from a historical record being inspected.
prompt: Append 100 fixture events while the user reads an older row, preserving position and keyboard focus.

name: Microsoft Presidio
fit: Identify and anonymize selected sensitive fields in text before secondary use.
tradeoff: Recognition varies by language and entity. Test local names and account formats with synthetic fixtures.
prompt: Compare missed and unnecessary redactions on approved Arabic and English examples.

name: TruffleHog
fit: Check authorized repositories and build inputs for exposed secrets as part of release hygiene.
tradeoff: Treat findings as sensitive and establish who can rotate affected credentials.
prompt: Specify a release gate and the incident owner for a seeded test credential without printing the value.

name: OWASP Threat Dragon
fit: Document system data flows, trust boundaries and defensive controls during design.
tradeoff: A diagram goes stale as tools and data sources change. Review it alongside the deployment diff.
prompt: Trace a customer lookup and an approval through the system and identify the enforcement point on each boundary.

name: in-toto
fit: Record and verify attestations about how software artifacts were produced.
tradeoff: An attestation is only useful when deployment verifies trusted identities and the intended artifact digest.
prompt: Describe which release evidence the deployment checks before admitting a worker image.
